title: Policy engine: tier precedence with quota-aware spillback and regional steering
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Implement a policy-driven routing layer that enforces tier precedence (free -> paid -> enterprise) while making quota-aware decisions that allow soft spillback to compatible model variants and region-aware routing. Goal: reduce failed requests due to quota exhaustion, preserve enterprise SLAs, and minimize latency regressions for paid users by routing to best-fit variants and regions automatically.
background: Current routing makes hard rejections when a tenant's tier quota is exhausted which causes poor UX for free users and spiky errors for paid customers during transient quota shortages. We need an admission + spillback strategy that: preserves enterprise latency/throughput guarantees, gives paid users degraded-but-usable model variants rather than hard errors, and routes to alternative regions when local capacity is constrained.
design_goals: 1) Respect tier precedence and contractual guarantees. 2) Soft-degrade for lower tiers instead of immediate reject when feasible. 3) Make routing decisions quota-aware at request-time with low overhead. 4) Support region affinity and cross-region spillover with cost/latency tradeoffs. 5) Provide observability and toggles for canary rollout.
proposed_design: - Policy layer sits between admission controller and scheduler. - On request arrival evaluate: tenant tier, remaining credit balance, configured min-SLO for tier, allowed fallback families. - If tenant quota insufficient: consult fallback table for compatible quantized/low-latency model variants (e.g., fp16 -> int8) and alternative regions. - Score candidates by composite metric: weighted(latency_estimate, cost_delta, model_quality_penalty). - Enforce hard blocks only for enterprise tier SLA violations. - Emit events: routed_variant, routed_region, admission_decision, reason_code.
acceptance_criteria: - No hard 4xx quota-exhaustion responses for paid tenants in controlled canary; instead 80% should be spilled to fallback variants when available. - Enterprise-tier requests maintain 95th pct latency within 10% of baseline under test load. - Free-tier requests show measurable fallbacks to cheaper variants rather than immediate rejections. - Dashboard exposes per-tenant spillback rate, routing decisions, and credit consumption timeline.
technical_notes: - Use existing credit-store API (reads at request-time) with local LRU cache to avoid added p99 overhead. - Score computation must be O(1) with small constant; keep candidate set < 4 variants/regions. - Add new reason codes for metrics: REQ_SPILLBACK_MODEL, REQ_SPILLBACK_REGION, REQ_REJECT_HARD_SLA. - Ensure KV cache compatibility for model-variant selection: variants within same architecture must share prefix cache strategy or eviction will spike latency.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated behind 'policy-tier-spillback'. 2) Internal traffic canary: 5% of non-critical tenants routing to policy for 2 days. 3) Paid customers opt-in A/B: 10% traffic. 4) Monitor spillback_rate, latency_delta, error_rate for 48h intervals. 5) Gradual ramp to 50% then full when metrics stable. 6) Emergency rollback via console toggle.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for scoring, fallback table resolution, and reason code mapping. - Integration tests: simulate quota exhaustion scenarios for free/paid/enterprise and assert expected admissions/redirects. - Load test: synthetic tenants under quota burst; measure p50/p95 for enterprise. - Chaos test: region outage simulation to validate cross-region spillover retains correctness.
monitoring_and_metrics: Emit the following metrics: routing.spillback.count, routing.spillback.by_tier, routing.routed_variant.latency_histogram, routing.routed_region.latency_histogram, routing.reject.count.by_reason. Create dashboard with per-tier SLA view and alert if enterprise p95 > baseline*1.2 or spillback_rate for paid > 40%.
security_and_compliance: No new data plane changes. Ensure audit log entries include original tenant_id, chosen_variant, chosen_region for compliance auditing. KMS keys unchanged. Security review not required for initial rollout but will be requested if cross-account data plane changes are introduced.
migration_notes: - Populate fallback table from model onboarding metadata (model_family -> compatible_variants). - Update model catalog with variant quality scores. - Backfill historical metrics to set reasonable scoring weights before wide rollout.
open_questions: What exact quality penalty thresholds do PMs accept for paid vs free?
Do we allow cross-region spillover for enterprise only when latency delta < 100ms?
Should tenant-level override allow force-reject even when spillback available?
